author: claude
summary: Independent design-critique follow-up: fixed A11Y-3 (VoiceCatalogCard's card body was a giant role="button" nesting other interactive controls), H-4 (the Star icon meant three different things across surfaces, differentiated only by color), and H-5 (MultiSelect's filter chips didn't match the pill taxonomy hue used elsewhere on the Voices page).

files.change: A11Y-3: removed the single role="button"/tabIndex=0/onClick/onKeyDown from the card-body wrapper div (which nested the avatar's real play <button>, VoicePillRow's own "+N more" toggle button, and UntaggedBadge's click target -- invalid ARIA, interactive content inside a button). The wrapper is now a plain non-interactive div. The navigate-to-Voice-Lab (or, in select mode, toggle-selection) affordance moved to a real <button> wrapping just the voice name (new data-testid="voice-catalog-card-name-btn"; data-testid="voice-catalog-card-body" stays on the now-inert wrapper). Removed the now-unnecessary e.stopPropagation() calls on the avatar play button and the untagged-badge row (no longer needed since the parent has no click handler to bubble into). H-4: added a doc comment cross-referencing VariantSwitcher.tsx's icon differentiation (this card's app-default badge keeps the Star icon).

H-4: the per-variant-default control's icon changed from lucide's Star to BadgeCheck, so it no longer shares an icon shape with VoiceCatalogCard's app-default Star badge (previously the two were differentiated by color alone -- accent-blue vs. amber -- which the file's own prior doc comment already flagged as a collision risk). Updated the file header doc comment accordingly. No prop/behavior change beyond the icon swap (this edit landed on top of a concurrent, already-in-flight ARIA re-model of this same file -- see 2026-07-15-voices-round2-variant-switcher-aria-remodel.json for that unrelated change set).

H-5: added an optional `category?: PillCategory` prop (mirroring metadata/chip.tsx's existing pattern for the same problem in the metadata editor). When supplied, the trigger's selected-value chips render with `--pill-{category}-bg`/`-text` tokens (plus a `data-category` attribute) instead of the previous generic `--accent-glow`/`--accent` fill applied to every facet regardless of taxonomy. Omitting `category` preserves the prior generic accent styling exactly (for callers with no taxonomy facet, e.g. a free-form tag filter).

H-5: pass category="class"/"gender"/"age" to the three taxonomy-sourced MultiSelects so their selected chips match the VoicePill hues used elsewhere on the page (indigo/pink/amber, design-system.md §5). The free-form TAGS MultiSelect deliberately omits `category` and stays neutral/generic, matching how free tags render as ghost pills.

Updated card-body-click tests to target the new voice-catalog-card-name-btn testid instead of the old whole-body role="button". Added: a test that the body wrapper carries no role/tabIndex/click handler and a click on it does not navigate; a test that the name is a real, independently focusable <button>; a keyboard (Enter/Space via userEvent) activation test on the name button; and an H-4 test asserting the app-default badge renders lucide's Star icon.
Added an H-4 test asserting the variant-default control renders lucide's BadgeCheck icon, not Star.
Added H-5 tests: selected chips keep the generic accent styling with no category prop, and pick up the matching --pill-{category}-* tokens (plus data-category) when a category is supplied.
Added an H-5 test asserting CLASS/GENDER/AGE selected chips carry their facet's data-category and pill-hue styling, while the TAGS filter's selected chip stays generic/accent.

Fixed the pre-existing failure this same A11Y-3 change caused/exposed (flagged as out-of-scope in the concurrent VariantSwitcher ARIA-remodel changelog entry): updated the 'forwards onNavigateToLab ... (card body click)' test to click the new voice-catalog-card-name-btn testid instead of the now-inert voice-catalog-card-body wrapper.

out_of_scope_next: MultiSelectRow's dropdown-panel isSelected highlight (background: var(--accent-glow), color: var(--accent)) was left generic -- H-5's finding specifically named the trigger's summary chips, not the in-panel option-row highlight. Revisit if a future audit flags the option-row highlight as the same taxonomy-hue drift.
